title: Lesson 7: When You Drift
description: You will stumble. Every Christian does. This lesson shows that Jesus saves you and keeps you by grace, that obeying Him is how you show your love, and how to turn around when you fall: Stop, Turn, Walk.

blocks.text: You have walked through six lessons now. This last one is about the days you fall short, because every follower of Jesus does, and about what happens next. It begins with a shepherd.

blocks.alt: A shepherd climbs down a rocky hillside toward a lost sheep and lifts it onto his shoulders

blocks.title: The Shepherd Who Comes Looking
blocks.text:
Jesus told a story about a shepherd who had a hundred sheep. Picture one of them wandering off, not in rebellion and not by any plan, just drifting one patch of grass at a time, until it looks up and realizes it is alone.

"What man of you, having a hundred sheep, if he has lost one of them, does not leave the ninety-nine in the open country, and go after the one that is lost, until he finds it? And when he has found it, he lays it on his shoulders, rejoicing." (Luke 15:4-5)

Notice what the shepherd does. He does not wait for the sheep to find its way back. He does not stand at the gate shaking his head. He leaves everything and goes after the one. And when he finds it, he does not scold it. He puts it on his shoulders and carries it home, and then he calls his friends and neighbors to celebrate. Jesus finished the story this way: "Just so, I tell you, there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine righteous persons who need no repentance" (Luke 15:7).

Notice who does the work in this story. The sheep does not find its way home, and it does not earn its place back in the flock. The shepherd goes after it, carries it home, and celebrates. That is how Jesus saved you, and it is how He keeps you.
7.1 - When have you felt like the lost sheep, drifting without even realizing it?
Kept by Jesus, Not by Being Perfect

Many new Christians quietly wonder: if I sin after I am saved, am I still saved? Here is the good news. You were not saved by being good, and you do not stay saved by being good. It is all Jesus. He paid for your sin on the cross, and He holds on to you. Jesus said of His sheep, "I give them eternal life, and they will never perish, and no one will snatch them out of my hand" (John 10:28).

For by grace you have been saved through faith. And this is not your own doing; it is the gift of God, not a result of works, so that no one may boast. For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared beforehand, that we should walk in them.

Paul puts good works in their right place. They do not save you, but they do follow. You were saved for good works, not by them. Think of an apple tree. It does not grow apples to become an apple tree. It grows apples because it already is one.
7.2 - Have you ever felt you had to be good enough to stay saved?
Obedience Shows Your Love

So does obeying God matter? Very much. Jesus said, "If you love me, you will keep my commandments" (John 14:15). Obedience is not how you earn your place in God's family. It is how you show your love for the One who brought you in. You do not obey to stay saved. You obey because you are saved.

The Bible calls this growing in holiness: becoming more like Jesus, a little at a time. Some days you will fight sin hard, but you do not fight alone or on your own strength. The same grace that saved you trains you to say no to sin and yes to God (Titus 2:11-12), and the Holy Spirit lives in you to help.
When You Fall, Turn Around

You will still sin. "The righteous falls seven times and rises again" (Proverbs 24:16). What marks a follower of Jesus is not that they never fall but that they get back up and come home. The Bible calls that repentance.

Repentance means turning around. In the Old Testament the word means to turn back, and in the New Testament it means a change of mind that changes your direction. Picture a 180-degree turn: you were walking away from God, and now you turn and walk back toward Him. Paul described new believers who "turned to God from idols to serve the living and true God" (1 Thessalonians 1:9). Repentance is not a 360-degree spin, where you feel bad for a moment and keep walking the same way. It is a full turn home.

When you sin, you will hear two voices. Condemnation says, "You are a failure. Give up," and it pushes you away from God. Conviction is the Holy Spirit saying, "You are headed the wrong way. Come home," and it pulls you toward Him. If what you feel makes you want to run from God, that is not His voice.
Repentance has three simple steps: Stop, Turn, Walk.
You can make that turn in a few honest minutes on any day. In a later course you will learn a fuller tool called the Learning Circle. The promise underneath it does not change:
If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.

This week you will read John 21. Peter had denied Jesus three times, and after the resurrection Jesus met him on a beach. He did not shame Peter. He asked him, "Do you love me?" and then said, "Follow me" (John 21:17, 19). Failure was not the end of Peter's story. Love and following were the next chapter.
Bring It Into the Light

God also gives you His people. "Therefore, confess your sins to one another and pray for one another, that you may be healed" (James 5:16). You do not tell a friend in order to be forgiven, because Jesus already settled that. You tell someone so you do not carry your sin alone. Talking about sin out loud can feel scary the first time, and that is normal. Find a mature believer you trust. If you are going through these lessons with someone, this is a good place to slow down and ask your questions.
7.3 - What questions about sin, forgiveness, or obeying God do you want to talk through?
Looking Back on the Journey

You have now walked through all seven lessons of Starting in Discipleship: following Jesus, salvation and baptism, prayer, the Bible, the church, sharing your faith, and getting back up when you fall. These are not just topics. They are the foundations of a life being changed by the grace of God.
7.4 - As you look back on all seven lessons and the Gospel of John, what has changed in your walk with God?
Lesson 7 Review

Jesus saved you by grace, and He keeps you by grace. Like the shepherd, He goes after you when you wander and carries you home. Obedience does not earn His love; it shows your love for Him. You do not obey to stay saved. You obey because you are saved. And when you fall, bring it into the light with someone you trust, and make the 180: Stop, Turn, Walk.

You have completed the Starting in Discipleship course. The next step is Growing Deep, where you will go deeper into your identity in Christ, explore the cross, and learn practical tools for walking with God through every season.

blocks.heading: Introduction to John 19, 20, and 21
blocks.intro: In John 19-21, you will read the most important events in all of human history: the crucifixion, death, and resurrection of Jesus Christ. Take your time with these chapters, because this is the foundation that everything you have studied in this course is built on.
